Microsoft declares internal Code Red after nearly 24-hour Microsoft 365 outage

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (951 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that microsoft Corp.
  • Sources indicate that the outage on Nov.
  • Recent findings suggest that in a memo to staff on Friday, Jason Henderson, president of Microsoft 365 Core, described the outage as the most customer-affecting incident in the history of Exchange Online.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 18:44 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

Recent findings suggest that microsoft Corp. has declared an internal “Code Red” to overhaul how it prevents and responds to major service failures following the nearly 24-hour outage that took down Exchange Online and other Microsoft 365 services earlier this month, according to internal memos reviewed by Reuters today.

Sources indicate that the outage on Nov. 12 and 13 also disrupted Outlook, Teams and the Copilot artificial intelligence assistant, affecting governments from Australia and Japan to the U.S., delaying trading firms and disrupting airline communications. The designation signals the most severe and urgent level of alert inside Microsoft, according to the report.

Recent findings suggest that in a memo to staff on Friday, Jason Henderson, president of Microsoft 365 Core, described the outage as the most customer-affecting incident in the history of Exchange Online. “Code Red means that this is the highest priority work for our team,” Henderson wrote. He also conceded that the work done over the years had not been enough to protect the firm on the day of the outage.

In a recent development, engineers working the incident faced a “fog of war,” according to a separate memo sent on Monday by Amanda Silver, corporate vice president overseeing Microsoft 365 Core and Work IQ. Silver’s memo describes responders exchanging more than 11,000 messages across 11 Teams chats, with diagnostic data spread across fragmented internal tracking systems.

The Code Red covers five workstreams set out by Silver, including load shedding, geographic traffic partitioning and faster recovery mechanisms. Microsoft has also set a target of resolving future incidents worldwide within an hour, with AI agents to be used to help engineers diagnose system health data more promptly.

How long it takes to push out fixes is another concern raised by Henderson. Writing in an earlier memo this month, Henderson said one urgent production fix had taken five to six days to reach worldwide saturation, while for urgent security concerns the goal is to go from detection to safe worldwide deployment within an hour, something he admitted the company has yet to achieve. Henderson also intends to hold daily meetings with the Substrate leadership team that oversees the engineering group responsible for the underlying Microsoft 365 services, along with weekly reviews of the corrective work.

The outage itself was blamed by Microsoft on a defect introduced in July in a fix that had been prepared for its Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers. Under certain load conditions, lock contention inside an internal Windows process was found to exhaust processor and memory resources on the servers, leaving more than 80% of them unresponsive at the worst point, according to Microsoft’s preliminary post-incident report. Microsoft, whose Chief Executive Satya Nadella has publicly apologized for the disruption, has said the incident was not related to cyber activity or AI agents.

Silver’s memo also cites Charles Lamanna, executive vice president of Copilot, Agents and Platform, who told a Code Red review that the affected component had seen “roughly ten years’ worth of acceptable failures.”.

Industry observers note that speed comes with its own risks, according to security experts. “What concerns me is that speed and safety pull against each other,” Waseem Ahmed, head of engineering at AI security operations startup Secure.com, told SiliconANGLE. In his view, a pipeline able to push a fix to the world in an hour “can push a mistake in an hour.”.

Geographic traffic partitioning, which Ahmed said limits how far a single bad change can travel, is the one of the five Code Red workstreams he would be watching.

Darin Fredde, senior director and offensive security evangelist at autonomous penetration testing company Ridge Security Technology Inc., noted that “an organization may have a recovery plan but still struggle to execute it if the tools needed to recover depend on the service that has failed.”.

Real Estate Tycoon Mauricio Umansky Reveals What Luxury Buyers Want Most—From Secluded Estates to Private Spas

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1226 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realtor

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mauricio Umansky has a read on what makes a multimillion-dollar home irresistible.
  • Industry observers note that for some of his buyers, it’s enough acreage to put real distance between them and the neighbors.
  • “Privacy is becoming a bigger priority for luxury buyers,” The Agency founder revealed while speaking to Mansion Global.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Umansky has a read on what makes a multimillion-dollar home irresistible.

Industry observers note that for some of his buyers, it’s enough acreage to put real distance between them and the neighbors. For others, it’s the luxury of stepping into a sauna or taking a cold plunge without leaving home.

“Privacy is becoming a bigger priority for luxury buyers,” The Agency founder revealed while speaking to Mansion Global.

He remarked buyers are drawn to properties where they can retreat from view, feel secure, and build a wellness routine around amenities such as a private gym or spa.

Umansky is putting his read on the market to work in Miami’s Edgewater neighborhood, where he is leading sales for HQ Residences Miami.

In a recent development, the project brings together singer Marc Anthony, hospitality entrepreneur Sam Nazarian, and SBE. Its pitch borrows from the hotel world, pairing private residences with wellness amenities, places for neighbors to gather, and an emphasis on service.

Even at the top of the market, buyers are watching what they pay. Umansky said there’s room to negotiate in some areas, while a well-priced home in a coveted location can still draw strong interest.

He recommended finding an agent who knows the neighborhood and being ready to act when a property comes along that you can see yourself living in for years.

Umansky’s own homes span Los Angeles, La Quinta, CA, and Aspen, CO.

In a recent development, los Angeles gives him access to city life, while La Quinta offers the appeal of a slower pace, sunny days, and a round of golf. In Aspen, the draw extends from ski season to summers in the mountains and the sense of community he finds there.

If he were to add another address, Umansky mentioned he could picture himself in Europe.

He singled out the South of France, Italy, and Spain, with particular affection for Madrid. Miami also appeals to him as a place to own a home, especially after spending more time in the city through his work on HQ Residences.

Industry observers note that the broker also reflected on what TV has done for his business. Appearances on “Buying Beverly Hills,” “Dancing With the Stars,” and “Special Forces” have introduced him to people he might never have met through real estate alone, he said, and brought more attention to The Agency.

According to recent reports, the trade-off is that some people form an impression of him from what they see on camera. He said he wants his reputation to rest on his work as an agent and the trust he earns from clients.

As for the prospect of running for mayor, Umansky spoke about what he would focus on if he pursued the job.

Industry observers note that “Los Angeles is my home, and I care deeply about its future,” he told Mansion Global. He said he’d look at how the city handles housing approvals and development, with the goal of making it easier to build and attracting more investment and jobs.

Recent findings suggest that the candid glimpse into what wealthy buyers want comes one week after his stepdaughter, Farrah Aldjufrie—who is also Kyle Richards' daughter—gave birth to a baby boy. The arrival came three months after Aldjufrie revealed the baby's father is Zach Goldsmith, her "Buying Beverly Hills" co-star and fellow The Agency agent.

The 37-year-old property mogul, who is the daughter of Richards and her ex-husband, Guraish Aldjufrie, shared the news in July that she was expecting her first child.

Then, one month later, she hard-debuted her relationship with Goldsmith while sharing a video of the two of them celebrating their gender reveal.

A source told Page Six that the TV alum has welcomed her son, though Aldjufrie has yet to confirm the news herself.

The pregnancy marked a joyful personal milestone for the real estate mogul, whose professional achievements have often played out in front of TV audiences.

Sources indicate that aldjufrie had previously revealed how Umansky helped to cultivate her love of real estate. In a 2016 interview with The Daily Dish, she remarked that as a child, she used to drive around L.A. with her stepfather to tour listings, fascinated by everything that went into selling them.

It has been revealed that “I always have been interested in real estate since I was a little kid. I’d drive around to open houses with my mom and Mauricio when I was 6, 7, 8 years old. I’d love to see all the houses,” she stated.

“I know L.A. geographically really, really well, having grown up here. I was an only child for the first eight years, so I spent a lot of time with them and was very interested in everything Mauricio was doing. But I have my own love for property and being in L.A. There's some of the most amazing properties and lifestyles in the world.”.

According to her profile on The Agency's website, Aldjufrie became an agent in 2013—and has since helped the firm to achieve "over $5 billion in real estate sales.".

Interestingly, while she continues her professional and personal relationship with The Agency's founder, Umansky, her mother made clear just a few months ago that she believes she is entitled to a significant chunk of her estranged husband's empire—telling her Bravo co-stars that she will fight to claim her half of the business that she says she helped to build should the couple end up filing for divorce.

In a recent development, umansky founded The Agency alongside Billy Rose and Blair Chang in 2011, 15 years after he wed Richards. By May 2022, the business had facilitated more than $57 billion in real estate sales, according to Forbes.

According to The Agency's website, the organization operates more than 145 offices in 14 countries, while Umansky's bio notes that he has "achieved nearly $5 billion in real estate sales and holds the distinction of selling the most homes in the country priced above $20 million.

"He has represented some of the world's most noteworthy properties, including the Playboy Mansion—the first house in L.A. to sell above the $100 million mark—the Walt Disney Estate, and residences owned by Michael Jackson, Michael Jordan and Prince.".

Indeed, in the 15 years since it was founded, The Agency has built up a wealth of clients, including Lady Gaga, LeBron James, and Ben Affleck.

While it's unclear whether Richards would seek to be involved in the day-to-day running of the business that she hopes to claim a 50% share in, it's likely that she could be in line for a hefty payout if Umansky wishes to keep The Agency to himself.

However, Richards noted that she isn't quite ready to pull the plug on their marriage once and for all.

Tech Report: Mastering the Art: How Real Estate Agents Should Write Facebook Ad Copy

📅 07 Jun 2023 | ⏱️ 4 min read (722 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realtybiznews

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, in the digital age, social media platforms have become powerful tools for real estate agents to market their listings and attract potential clients.
  • Recent findings suggest that the first step to writing compelling Facebook ad copy is gaining a deep understanding of your target audience.
  • The headline is the first element of your Facebook ad copy that people will see.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, in the digital age, social media platforms have become powerful tools for real estate agents to market their listings and attract potential clients. Among the various platforms available, Facebook remains a dominant force with its massive user base and advertising capabilities. To stand out in the competitive real estate market, agents must not only create compelling visual content but also craft persuasive ad copy that engages and captivates their target audience. In this article, we will delve into the key elements and strategies for writing effective Facebook ad copy, equipping real estate agents with the knowledge to maximize their advertising efforts and generate leads.

Recent findings suggest that the first step to writing compelling Facebook ad copy is gaining a deep understanding of your target audience. By knowing their demographics, preferences, and pain points, you can tailor your copy to resonate with their needs and desires. Conduct thorough market research, utilize Facebook's audience insights, and analyze data from previous campaigns to gather valuable information about your target audience.

The headline is the first element of your Facebook ad copy that people will see. It needs to be attention-grabbing and compelling enough to entice people to read further. Use action-oriented words, emphasize unique selling propositions, and create a sense of urgency to pique the audience's curiosity and encourage them to click on your ad.

When writing Facebook ad copy, it's crucial to highlight the benefits of the property or service you're promoting, rather than merely listing its features. Benefits explain how the property or service can improve the lives of potential buyers or renters. By emphasizing the value and advantages, you can create an emotional connection with your audience and motivate them to take action.

In a recent development, storytelling is a powerful tool for capturing the attention of your audience and making your Facebook ad copy more relatable. Craft a compelling narrative that showcases the unique aspects of the property or the positive experiences of previous clients. Engaging stories can evoke emotions, create a sense of authenticity, and build trust with potential clients.

It has been revealed that in the fast-paced world of social media, attention spans are limited. To ensure your Facebook ad copy is effective, keep it concise and clear. Use short sentences and paragraphs, bullet points, and subheadings to enhance readability. Avoid jargon and technical terms that may confuse or alienate your audience.

According to recent reports, social proof, such as testimonials, reviews, or success stories, can significantly influence potential clients' decision-making process. Incorporate social proof into your Facebook ad copy to build credibility and trust. Highlight positive feedback from satisfied clients or showcase awards and recognition you've received in the real estate industry.

It has been revealed that to encourage immediate action from your audience, create a sense of urgency in your Facebook ad copy. Limited-time offers exclusive deals, or a countdown timer can instill a fear of missing out (FOMO) and prompt potential clients to take the desired action promptly.

An effective call-to-action (CTA) is vital to prompt customers to take the desired action, whether it's contacting you, visiting a landing page, or scheduling a property viewing. Use action verbs, provide clear instructions, and create a sense of urgency to motivate users to click on your CTA button.

Continuous testing and optimization are essential for improving the performance of your Facebook ad copy. Create multiple variations of your ad copy, test them against each other, and analyze the results. Fine-tune your copy based on metrics such as click-through rates (CTR), conversion rates, and engagement levels to identify what resonates best with your audience.

Writing compelling Facebook ad copy is a crucial skill for real estate agents looking to excel in their digital marketing efforts. By understanding their target audience, crafting attention-grabbing headlines, focusing on benefits, incorporating storytelling techniques, and utilizing social proof, agents can create persuasive and engaging copy that captivates potential clients. Remember to keep your copy concise and clear, create a sense of urgency, and use compelling calls to action. Through A/B testing and continuous optimization, agents can refine their ad copy to maximize its effectiveness. By mastering the art of writing Facebook ad copy, real estate agents can unlock the full potential of social media advertising and boost their success in the competitive real estate market.

#110737. Powerful new weight-loss drug helps patients cut knee pain in half

Powerful new weight-loss drug helps patients cut knee pain in half

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1156 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, for people living with painful knee osteoarthritis (OA), even simple activities like walking, climbing stairs, or getting out of a chair can become a struggle.
  • Sources indicate that the two phase 3 trials, led by Northwestern University, included more than 1,000 participants in total.
  • According to recent reports, the benefits extended beyond weight loss and improved knee pain.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, for people living with painful knee osteoarthritis (OA), even simple activities like walking, climbing stairs, or getting out of a chair can become a struggle. Excess body weight can make these challenges even worse. Now, two major clinical trials suggest that a powerful experimental weight-loss drug could provide substantial relief.

Sources indicate that the two phase 3 trials, led by Northwestern University, included more than 1,000 participants in total. People receiving the highest dose of retatrutide, an experimental injectable weight-loss medication, lost an average of about 25% of their body weight. When researchers combined the findings from both trials, they found that approximately two-thirds of participants treated with retatrutide reported a reduction in knee pain of at least 50%. By comparison, only 38% of those given a placebo experienced that level of relief.

According to recent reports, the benefits extended beyond weight loss and improved knee pain. Participants also showed reductions in blood pressure, blood lipid levels, and inflammation throughout the body.

Industry observers note that findings from both studies were published on Nov. 8 in the New England Journal of Medicine.

Recent findings suggest that "The findings are really saying for people who are overweight and have OA, if you lose a significant amount of weight with this treatment, there is a good chance that you're going to get a meaningful reduction in your knee pain," remarked corresponding author Dr. Thomas Schnitzer, professor of physical medicine and rehabilitation, anesthesiology and medicine (rheumatology) at Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine.

"A major factor is that you're loading your knees less and therefore, there's less pain and it allows you to increase your function.".

Philip Conaghan, a study co-author and professor of musculoskeletal medicine at the University of Leeds in the United Kingdom, presented results from one of the trials, TRIUMPH-4, on Nov. 8 at the American College of Rheumatology annual meeting in Orlando, Florida. Findings from the second trial, TRIUMPH-1-OA, were scheduled for presentation during a separate poster session that same day.

A Potential Latest Treatment for Millions With Knee Osteoarthritis.

Sources indicate that painful knee osteoarthritis affects approximately 5% of Americans (15 million people). Available treatments range from physical therapy and medications applied to the skin to oral anti-inflammatory drugs such as ibuprofen and Voltaren. Other options include opioids and corticosteroid injections, although the relief provided by steroid injections generally lasts only a short time.

Weight loss is another established way to ease symptoms. Previous studies have shown that losing 5% to 10% of body weight through changes in diet and exercise can improve knee osteoarthritis pain. However, Schnitzer explained that losing more than 10% through these approaches alone is often challenging. For people already struggling with painful knees, exercising enough to achieve substantial weight loss can be especially difficult.

Sources indicate that retatrutide could offer another approach. Developed by Eli Lilly, the experimental medication is administered as a once-weekly injection and works differently from existing GLP-1 medications such as semaglutide and tirzepatide.

While those drugs act on one or two hormone receptors and typically produce weight reductions of 10% to 20%, retatrutide activates receptors associated with three different naturally occurring hormones. In the clinical trials, participants lost approximately 20% to 25% of their body weight, depending on the dose. Eli Lilly scientists also contributed to the research as study co-authors.

"Participants had remarkable responses," Schnitzer stated. "Many of the people in this study lost considerable amounts of weight, with a few losing up to a hundred pounds or more.".

Why Diet and Exercise Still Matter.

Despite the encouraging findings, Schnitzer emphasized that lifestyle changes should remain the starting point for people who are overweight and have painful knee osteoarthritis.

Recent findings suggest that improving eating habits, increasing physical activity, and making other sustainable lifestyle adjustments can help reduce symptoms without the expense of newer weight-loss medications. These strategies also avoid side effects associated with GLP-1 drugs, including gastrointestinal problems and muscle loss.

In a recent development, maintaining muscle strength is particularly crucial for people with knee osteoarthritis because the muscles surrounding the joint help support and stabilize it. Losing too much muscle could therefore create additional challenges for patients who already have difficulty moving comfortably.

Sources indicate that for individuals who cannot achieve sufficient weight loss through lifestyle changes and continue to experience significant knee pain, Schnitzer believes retatrutide could become a valuable option if it receives approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

Could the Drug Also Slow Knee Arthritis Progression?

Although the trials demonstrated substantial improvements in weight and pain, several notable questions remain unanswered.

One of the biggest is whether retatrutide does more than relieve symptoms. Researchers still do not know if the drug can slow the underlying progression of knee osteoarthritis enough to reduce the likelihood that patients will eventually need knee replacement surgery. People who already required a knee replacement were excluded from the trials.

"That would be the goal here to say you can reduce people's pain, and you can stop the progression of their osteoarthritis," Schnitzer said.

In a recent development, another unanswered question is whether retatrutide might benefit people with painful knee osteoarthritis who are not overweight. Because the trials did not include these patients, further studies will be needed to determine whether they could experience similar improvements.

Researchers are also interested in understanding how much of the pain relief comes directly from weight loss and how much might be related to the drug's effects on inflammation.

It has been revealed that "These drugs are believed to have significant anti-inflammatory activity, but the mechanism is not entirely known," Schnitzer said. "Whether cutting down inflammation in the joint is also important in addition to reducing load needs more research, so this is still a first step, in my view. I've been working in the OA field for a long time, and I think this opens up opportunities to do a lot more studies to understand the condition better.".

How Researchers Measured Knee Pain Relief.

To evaluate changes in symptoms, the research teams used the Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Arthritis Index (WOMAC) Pain index, a standardized tool for assessing osteoarthritis pain.

It has been revealed that during study visits, participants rated their pain on a scale from 0 to 10. They also used a mobile app to record their pain levels each day, allowing researchers to track how symptoms changed throughout treatment.

The study is titled, "Retatrutide Once Weekly in Adults with Knee Osteoarthritis Pain and Obesity.".

Materials provided by Northwestern University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

Ethereum is preparing to rebuild some of its most key security foundations. The Ethereum Foundation has doubled its protocol security team as developers accelerate a cryptographic overhaul aimed at surviving increasingly capable artificial intelligence and quantum computers.

Ethereum researchers want to change how validators sign messages, how users authorize transactions, and how Ethereum handles data commitments. The changes reach deep into the machinery protecting the blockchain.

The Foundation has put the transition on an aggressive timeline, targeting December 2028. Researchers say the work is harder than the Merge, leaving Ethereum with a serious engineering challenge. Ethereum security is becoming a race against technology that keeps improving.

According to recent reports, quantum computers have dominated Ethereum’s long-term cryptographic concerns, and AI is now changing the urgency of that conversation. The Foundation indicates AI models are already finding software vulnerabilities faster than humans can review them. Researchers expect those capabilities to improve, potentially extending into cryptographic research and the mathematical assumptions protecting blockchain networks.

Industry observers note that ethereum isn’t waiting for a machine to crack its cryptography. Developers are preparing for a future where today’s security assumptions could become less reliable, while attackers gain increasingly powerful tools.

The proposed overhaul moves away from elliptic-curve cryptography toward hash-based alternatives. Researchers believe hash-based cryptography offers a more conservative foundation because Ethereum already relies heavily on hash security.

The transition would affect three major areas. Validators would use hash-based keys, wallets would gain a pathway toward hash-based signatures, and data commitments used by rollups would change. This means infrastructure across Ethereum would need to adapt, from staking operators and wallets to multisignature systems.

The challenge is making these changes without breaking the network people already depend on. Bigger signatures could increase hardware demands, while existing tools built around current cryptography would need substantial updates.

Discover: The Crypto Presales This Q4 2026.

In a recent development, ethereum’s Merge in September 2022 replaced proof-of-work mining with proof-of-stake while keeping the blockchain running. Developers spent years preparing client software, testing networks, and coordinating the transition.

The upcoming overhaul could prove even more difficult. It touches cryptographic components that sit beneath Ethereum’s consensus, account systems, and data infrastructure. Developers have less time, and moving rapidly creates more opportunities for mistakes.

Industry observers note that that’s why doubling the protocol security team is needed. Formal verification, independent reviews, and extensive testing will need to keep pace with development. A rushed cryptographic migration could create exactly the vulnerabilities Ethereum is trying to eliminate.

The Foundation’s December 2028 target also puts pressure on the wider ecosystem. Wallet developers, staking pools, rollup teams, and node operators will eventually face migration work of their own. The upgrade isn’t something Ethereum’s core developers can finish in isolation.

Ethereum’s bet is that preparing early beats waiting for the threat to become obvious. That means potentially delaying other features, rewriting familiar infrastructure, and asking developers to tackle difficult changes before a practical quantum threat arrives.

This simple habit is linked to a 33% lower risk of Alzheimer's

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Reading for enjoyment may offer far more than entertainment.
  • Researchers at the University of Cambridge are working with The Queen's Reading Room, a charity established by Her Majesty The Queen, to raise awareness of these benefits across all age groups.
  • According to recent reports, cambridge psychiatry researchers Professor Barbara Sahakian and Dr.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Reading for enjoyment may offer far more than entertainment. Whether someone prefers a classic Jane Austen novel or a Heartstopper graphic novel, research suggests that reading for pleasure is associated with better mental health, stronger empathy, and a lower risk of dementia.

Researchers at the University of Cambridge are working with The Queen's Reading Room, a charity established by Her Majesty The Queen, to raise awareness of these benefits across all age groups. Their collaboration is part of the National Year of Reading, an initiative encouraging more people to make reading part of their lives.

According to recent reports, cambridge psychiatry researchers Professor Barbara Sahakian and Dr. Christelle Langley began exploring the subject while writing their 2025 book, Brain Boost: Healthy Habits for a Happier Life. They discovered that reading for enjoyment was connected to a remarkably wide range of positive outcomes, yet the amount of research specifically examining these benefits was surprisingly limited.

According to recent reports, in a review published in Psychological Medicine, Sahakian and Langley joined Vicki Perrin, CEO of The Queen's Reading Room, to examine the available evidence. Their findings suggest that the format and type of reading matter less than the enjoyment people get from it. They also highlight how reading together, whether through book clubs or parents sharing stories with children, can provide additional benefits.

Professor Sahakian remarked: "Reading is a great way to support our brain health, develop notable cognitive skills and boost our well-being. It's something we ought to be encouraging from an early age, given the increasing evidence of its benefits, particularly to children, but really, it's never too late to start, and it can bring benefits throughout our lives and into old age.".

Reading Early in Life Is Linked to Better Brain Development.

Despite the growing evidence of its advantages, reading for enjoyment has become less common among young people. Surveys indicate that reading rates among children and teenagers have fallen to their lowest recorded levels, with particularly steep challenges among teenage boys and children from disadvantaged backgrounds.

It has been revealed that even children who are least enthusiastic about reading recognize that it can help them academically. Nearly half acknowledge that books and other reading materials can introduce them to unfamiliar words or teach them something upcoming.

It has been revealed that one of the most compelling studies examined more than 10,000 young people. Conducted by Sahakian, Langley, and their colleagues, the research found that children who started reading for pleasure at an early age tended to perform better in several important areas. These included attention, memory, and executive functioning, the mental abilities involved in planning, decision-making, and managing behavior.

Early readers also revealed stronger academic performance, experienced fewer mental health problems, and were more likely to develop healthier daily routines. In particular, they tended to get more sleep and spend less time using screens.

Industry observers note that dr. Langley said: "Given how beneficial reading for pleasure is at a young age, we should be doing everything we can to introduce children and young people to reading. The crucial thing is to find something they'd really enjoy reading about - it might be a TV program or a game - and use this as a way in. Reading comics and graphic novels could also be a helpful introduction as they might be seen as less intimidating, maybe less boring, than novels.".

The academic advantages may extend beyond language and literacy. Studies have also connected reading with stronger mathematical performance. Researchers suggest this relationship may arise because both activities rely on some of the same mental abilities, including language processing, memory, and executive function.

Just Five Minutes of Reading May Reduce Stress.

The benefits of reading do not disappear after childhood. Among adults, surveys have associated reading for enjoyment with improved emotional well-being, greater relaxation, and reduced stress. Readers also tend to report more empathy, a deeper understanding of other people, and greater openness to viewpoints different from their own.

For many people, books are an especially appealing way to unwind. Reading ranks as the most popular approach to stress relief, with nearly two in five adults (38%) identifying it as their preferred way to relax.

According to recent reports, A neuroscience study commissioned by The Queen's Reading Room in 2024 found that spending just five minutes reading fiction could lower stress by as much as 20%. The study also reported improvements in concentration and problem-solving abilities, along with a reduced sense of loneliness.

Industry observers note that books may even provide more comfort than some traditional relaxation habits. In one survey, more respondents stated they turned to reading (35%) for comfort than to drinking wine (31%) or taking a hot bath (10%).

Reading Linked to Lower Dementia and Alzheimer's Risk.

In a recent development, as people get older, the potential advantages of reading may become especially meaningful. Research has associated mentally stimulating leisure activities, including reading, with slower cognitive decline and a reduced likelihood of developing dementia.

Recent findings suggest that one study followed nearly 5,500 adults aged 55 and older for five years. Participants who regularly took part in activities such as reading were significantly less likely to develop cognitive impairment during the study period.

It has been revealed that another investigation reported an even more striking association. People who read newspapers, magazines, and books had a 33% lower risk of Alzheimer's disease.

These findings suggest that keeping the mind engaged through reading may support cognitive health in later life. However, the researchers emphasize that most of the available studies identify associations rather than proving that reading itself prevents dementia.

How Reading May Change the Structure of the Brain.

In a recent development, what could explain the many benefits associated with reading? Brain imaging research offers some intriguing clues.

Studies have identified differences in brain structure associated with reading, particularly in regions responsible for language, learning, emotional regulation, and executive control. These differences include greater brain volume and larger cortical areas in certain regions, as well as thicker cortex in areas vital for language processing.

Researchers have also observed stronger connections within the brain's white matter, which helps different regions communicate and supports the processing of language.

Although much of this evidence is correlational, some research suggests that reading-related training can directly influence the brain's physical structure.

It has been revealed that in one small study involving 11 children with dyslexia between the ages of 7 and 11, researchers tested an eight-week training program designed to strengthen reading abilities. The exercises involved mental imagery, articulation, and tracing letters, combinations of letters, and words.

In a recent development, following the program, the children demonstrated significant improvements in reading skills. Brain scans also revealed increases in gray matter volume in important regions, providing evidence that reading interventions can be accompanied by measurable structural changes in the brain.

Why Reading Together May Offer Even Greater Benefits.

Reading does not have to be a solitary activity. Researchers suggest that sharing books with other people can add a valuable social dimension, creating opportunities for connection and potentially improving both mental and physical well-being.

The Queen's Reading Room has made this idea a central part of its mission. Introduced on social media in January 2021, the initiative originally provided a way for people to exchange book recommendations and stay connected during pandemic lockdowns.

Industry observers note that it has since expanded into an international community reaching more than 12 million people across 184 countries. Through its flagship festival, neuroscience research, and other programs, the charity works to make reading a more prominent part of everyday life.

Its activities also extend to homeless shelters and domestic violence refuges, where shared reading is used as a therapeutic resource to help people during recovery.

The social connections created through reading groups may be particularly valuable for older adults, who can face increased isolation and reduced opportunities to participate in physically demanding activities.

In a recent development, professor Sahakian said: "Shared reading groups and book clubs appear to provide additional benefits through social interaction. They can help people feel less isolated and more connected to others, which has been shown to reduce the risk of dementia.

"While these clubs can be fun and beneficial at any age, they're perfect for older people who may not be so mobile - they might not be able to go out as an exercise group or a cycling group, but a reading group is something most people can enjoy.".

Recent findings suggest that the researchers' overall message is that people can benefit from reading at any stage of life. Whether someone enjoys novels, newspapers, comics, or stories shared with friends, making time for reading may help support cognitive health, emotional well-being, and social connection.

Vicki Perrin, CEO of The Queen's Reading Room, added: "At The Queen's Reading Room, we have seen first-hand the transformative power of individual and shared reading to change lives. Books truly do make life better, and we're excited to do our bit to help everyone, everywhere, make more room for reading.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Malin Akerman has a private disco in her new Connecticut home, complete with a mixing deck and a smoke machine.

But ask the star of “The Hunting Wives” where she’s happiest in the house, and she’ll point you to a piece of living room furniture.

“Plopping down on our significant pink couch in the living room with my family,” the actress told The Wall Street Journal when he asked about her favorite spot.

It has been revealed that akerman, 48, moved to Connecticut in July with her husband, actor Jack Donnelly, and her son, Sebastian, 13. The family settled into a modern house built in 1988.

“The interior has an inviting flow, and all the rooms are cozy,” she said.

It has been revealed that one room in particular gives her a good excuse to send out invitations. Alongside the DJ equipment, Akerman has a disco ball and a laser. “I love to DJ, dance and have friends over for parties,” she mentioned.

Recent findings suggest that anyone who ever danced at Akerman’s house in Los Angeles might recognize the decor. In May, when she listed her longtime Hollywood Hills home for $2.9 million, she told Elle Decor that her disco ball would be coming east.

Industry observers note that she had a suggestion for whoever bought the place, too. “I sincerely hope the next owners put in a disco ball,” she stated.

Akerman found that California home while working at a downtown L.A. restaurant. A regular learned she was looking for a rental and offered to show her a house he owned with his brother.

According to recent reports, she spent three years there as a tenant before buying it in 2008. Over the years, she added a pool and turned the unfinished lower level into a primary suite that opened onto the garden, according to Elle Decor.

Staying at one address for two decades was a departure for Akerman. Her first home was a studio in Stockholm.

When she was 2, her father, Magnus, had job offers in Toronto and Upcoming York. Her parents chose Canada, where the view from their townhouse gave their daughter something to do as she drifted off.

“At night, I fell asleep counting trains,” she told the Journal.

Her father returned to Sweden after her parents divorced. Akerman, then 6, stayed in Canada with her mother, Pia.

According to recent reports, at 12, she moved into a white house in Niagara-on-the-Lake, the Ontario town where her new stepfather had grown up. Two years later, the marriage ended. Her little brother, Marcus, went to live with his father. Akerman stayed with Pia.

“Given the friction, I don’t have many happy memories of the house,” she mentioned.

It has been revealed that as she and her mother moved, Akerman changed schools. A drama elective she picked as a high school freshman gave her a circle of friends.

“Drama provided me with community and stability,” she recalled.

When a manager later encouraged her to move to Los Angeles, her best friend, Laura, went with her. A friend from high school took them in.

Acting work was slow to materialize, but Akerman studied the craft, and a role opposite Lisa Kudrow in “The Comeback” helped launch her career.

Recent findings suggest that now it’s Sebastian who has a role to celebrate at home. Akerman revealed that her son landed a part in Hulu’s “Paradise” on his first audition.

In a recent development, as for how swiftly he might follow his mother into the family business, she kept her answer brief. “We’re taking it slow.”.

Akerman dates her turning point to her early 20s, when she began to feel confident with her longtime girlfriends in her corner. As she put it, “They made me feel more connected and provided emotional support.”.

According to recent reports, akerman will also soon be celebrating the season 2 premiere of "The Hunting Wives," which airs on Nov. 26.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • However, the companies have very different prospects going forward as they try to come to terms with the diverging fortunes of the artificial intelligence server and personal computer markets they serve.
  • Dell reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of $9.45 per share on revenue of $54.94 billion, a stunning result that blew past Wall Street’s expectations of just $6.59 per share in earnings and $49.32 billion in sales.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 18:48 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

Updated with Wednesday stock prices:.

It has been revealed that dell Technologies Inc. and HP Inc. delivered strong earnings and revenue beats as they posted their latest financial results today.

However, the companies have very different prospects going forward as they try to come to terms with the diverging fortunes of the artificial intelligence server and personal computer markets they serve.

Dell reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of $9.45 per share on revenue of $54.94 billion, a stunning result that blew past Wall Street’s expectations of just $6.59 per share in earnings and $49.32 billion in sales.

The firm’s revenue more than doubled from a year earlier thanks to the sky-high demand for the AI servers and related data center infrastructure equipment it sells. Dell’s Infrastructure Solutions Group delivered sales of $41.97 billion during the quarter, far in excess of the Street’s target of $35.27 billion. Of that, around $22 billion came from direct AI-optimized server sales, the company mentioned. That segment was up 291% annually.

“We are now a different firm, with the Infrastructure Solutions Group driving the vast majority of our profit and growth,” said Dell Vice Chairman and Chief Operating Officer Jeff Clarke (pictured). He added that Dell now has more than 7,500 customers buying its AI servers.

The Street liked what it saw, with Dell’s stock rising more than 3% after hours, putting the brakes on an 11% decline earlier, during the regular trading session. Upgrade: However, on another down day for tech stocks Wednesday, Dell’s shares were falling almost 8% before the market cut some of those losses and Dell was falling only a fraction of a point.

Dell’s performance in the quarter sets a latest precedent for infrastructure systems companies, remarked longtime technology industry analyst Dave Vellante, chief analyst at theCUBE Research, SiliconANGLE Media’s sister market research firm.

Sources indicate that “Dell has transformed from a PC company into a dominant enterprise infrastructure provider and industry bellwether,” he remarked. “What’s most astounding to me is that I’ve always considered AWS to be Dell’s most formidable competitor. Dell is now significantly larger than AWS on a trailing 12-month revenue basis and is growing at a rate that’s more than double that of AWS, Azure and on a par with Google Cloud.”.

Sources indicate that dell is raising its forecast for AI servers in the coming fiscal years, and now sees sales rising to a staggering $78 billion, ahead of the Street’s target of $74 billion. At present, the company has an even bigger order backlog of $132.3 billion for AI servers. “Every order is verified for access to capital, end customer quality, trade and export compliance and access to land and power,” Clarke told analysts in response to a question about the reliability of that backlog.

Vellante said Dell’s operating leverage is just as impressive, with its operating income, net profit and earnings per share all growing at rates over two-times its revenue growth.

“Its massive backlog and strong product execution allow it to be selective,” the analyst said. “Thus the quality of its revenue and its backlog is very high, and the company is well-positioned for the next several quarters. Current market signals point to a structural change in tech where vendors that are in a position to help customers transform and drive new levels of productivity are poised to win over the long term. We increasingly see Dell as one of those leaders.”.

In a recent development, besides servers, Dell still has a massive business in the PC market. Its Client Services Group was once the manufacturer’s biggest segment, but its revenue is now dwarfed by AI server sales. During the quarter, it generated revenue of $12.89 billion, below the Street’s forecast of $14.33 billion.

The reason for that miss is that the global PC market is currently enduring a sharp decline. Last month, Gartner Inc. reported a stunning 22% drop in global PC shipments in the third quarter, citing the increased costs of components such as memory chips, which have led to higher prices and compelled many people to hold onto their older laptops for longer.

In a recent development, the miserable state of PC sales makes HP’s latest quarterly results seem even more impressive than they were. However, the firm’s cautious outlook suggests that its incoming Chief Executive Emma Walmsley (pictured, right) will have her work cut out when she assumes the role full time on Jan. 4, when she’s slated to take over from interim CEO Bruce Broussard.

It has been revealed that HP reported fourth-quarter adjusted earnings of 83 cents per share, surpassing the analyst consensus estimate that called for a profit of just 75 cents per share. Revenue for the period came to $16 billion, up 9% and above the Street’s target of $15.4 billion.

HP’s stock briefly surged more than 17% after-hours, before promptly surrendering all of those gains in under an hour. It was down just under a percentage point at the time of writing. Update: On Wednesday, investors appeared to change their minds again, as the stock was rising more than 12%.

Investors had low expectations of HP given the shoddy state of the PC market. The firm has been trying to mitigate the situation somewhat by raising its prices, but it couldn’t stop its profit margins from declining in the quarter.

The market was eagerly anticipating HP’s guidance to try and get a lid on whether or not the PC market has any prospect of recovery in the near future, but the manufacturer disappointed by refusing to provide any. All it would say is that it forecasts free cash flow in the current quarter to be $3 billion, plus or minus $100 million. Analysts are targeting free cash flow of $3.3 billion.

In a recent development, HP hasn’t been helped by the fact that it has been without a CEO since PayPal Holdings Inc. surprisingly swooped in to poach its former leader Enrique Lores in February. Broussard has held the fort for close to nine months now, but the tech giant did at least finally name a successor in Walmsley, who will begin her tenure next year. She formerly led the pharmaceutical giant GSK Plc.

Walmsley has a tough act to follow, however, for Broussard has done rather well in his efforts to cope with the PC market downturn and the higher component costs. Although the stock was up and down today, it’s still up 25% in the year to date.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Let’s face it: The holiday season is when our ovens are working overtime.

Unfortunately, it’s also the prime time for an oven fire.

MoneyGeek recently analyzed seven years of fire department reports to the National Fire Incident Reporting System and compared each state's Thanksgiving Day cooking fires with its own average November day, from 2019 to 2025. Nationally, departments reported 3.72 times as many residential cooking fires on Thanksgiving.

And it's not just the turkey that could get ruined.

While a professional kitchen remodel averages $26,994, depending on the scope of the project and the location, according to Angi.com, fire damage might amp up that pricetag depending on whether cabinets, drywall, appliances, or partial finishes need to be removed and replaced.

Major structural damage can reach $100,000 if flames or water damaged wiring and plumbing or if the fire spread to adjacent rooms.

This is why experts recommend tried and true precautions homeowners can take to keep their home safe.

In the days leading up to the holidays, be sure to inspect the inside of your oven.

“Look specifically for older grease buildups,” says Steve Lockwood, owner of Mountain State Fire Protection, a fire safety equipment inspector and installer in Mesa, AZ.

“Over time, those can build up, become extremely hot, and they could ignite pretty easily.”.

If you’re someone who routinely stores items in your oven, be sure to empty the space entirely—before you preheat it.

“Often people don’t realize they have plastic cutting boards and casserole dishes with plastic lids stored in their oven,” Sam Taylor, disaster public affairs program manager with the American Red Cross, tells Realtor.com.

“You don’t want to run the risk of melting those items in the oven.”.

During the entire time you’re cooking a dish on your burners, stow all combustible materials away.

“Pay special attention to such items as plastic spatulas and utensils that can melt and catch fire, as well as wooden spoons, oven mitts, and paper products,” Taylor says.

Always make sure you’re not cooking foods on too-high temperatures, which can result in a fire; avoid dangerous bump-ins; and make sure pan handles don’t hang over the edge of the burners.

“This can cause the contents to spill and could cause burns or fire,” Lockwood claims. And never wear a shirt with long, loose sleeves while you’re cooking.

“If you’re working over an open flame, that sleeve can catch fire,” states Taylor. “I always recommend wearing a different top that doesn’t have any fabric hanging near a flame.”.

Whatever you do, never leave the house when your oven is on, Lockwood indicates.

“Where most people go wrong is walking away from the kitchen,” he notes. Instead, keep an eye on your oven at all times. Tip: If you have a newer digital stove, pay special attention.

“A lot of these burners can be accidentally turned on just by leaning over them,” Lockwood says. “That’s why it’s a good practice to put the stove into a lockout mode to avoid an accidental turn on.”.

Should a fire happen, keep the oven door closed, turn off the heat, reach for your kitchen extinguisher, and alert the authorities.

Recent findings suggest that “Opening the oven door feeds the fire with oxygen,” Lockwood claims. “In addition, while baking soda will work in a pinch, never use water on a grease fire.”.

And, if a pot on your burner catches fire, turn off the heat and put a lid or baking sheet on it immediately to smother the fire, he adds.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 18:49 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

According to recent reports, artificial intelligence infrastructure startup Marlowe AI Inc. has closed a huge $227 million seed round led by Accel.

Bessemer, Altimeter, Emergence Capital and a number of other institutional bakers chipped in as well. They were joined by a large group of angel investors that included the chief executives of Palo Alto Networks Inc, Uber Technologies Inc., Box Inc. and Dropbox Inc. GeekWire reported on Monday that Marlowe is valued at $1.15 billion.

In a recent development, marlowe was founded last year by CEO Dan Lewis and Chief Technology Officer Kutta Srinivasan. Lewis previously headed the Microsoft Corp. unit responsible for Copilot Studio, the tech giant’s AI agent development tool. Srinivasan was the techical lead of the tech giant’s AI infrastructure group.

Sources indicate that marlowe is building AI data centers for inference workloads. The firm will optimize each facility for a specific inference workload category by tailoring its chip mix, network configuration and software. Marlowe believes that its approach will provide better hardware efficiency than general-purpose graphics card clusters.

“Even modest gains in network architecture, power oversubscription, AI-driven fleet operations, and workload-specific inference optimization multiply to create a durable, 2-3x overall advantage in performance, availability, resiliency, and cost,” Lewis and Srinivasan wrote in Marlowe’s launch blog post.

Sources indicate that the firm aims to bring its first data center online  next month. It’s based on hardware from Etched Inc., an inference chip startup that was valued at $21 billion in August.

Graphics cards often use only a small fraction of their maximum clock speed to avoid overheating. Etched’s chip is less prone to overheating and can therefore operate at higher clock speeds, which boosts model performance. The organization notes that its accelerator provides “multiple times the FLOPs density” of graphics cards.

Etched ships its chips as part of custom-made inference racks. According to the company, the systems feature an interconnect that can perform some data movement tasks more than four times faster than competing silicon. Etched’s rack design also includes custom power management and cooling components.

In a recent development, marlowe’s second facility will come online in the second quarter of 2027. It will host racks based on Advanced Micro Devices Inc.’s Helios design. A Helios rack hosts 72 AMD graphics cards along with central processing units and Pensando data processing units, or DPUs. The DPUs offload networking tasks from the other chips to leave more computing capacity for AI models.

Industry observers note that helios racks’ networking and power delivery links are arranged in a configuration that reduces the need for manual cable maintenance. Additionally, the coolant lines feature a so-called quick-disconnect design. They can be plugged and unplugged without the specialized tools usually needed for the task.

Industry observers note that geekWire reported that Marlowe has also signed a letter of intent for a third data center. According to the publication, each of the firm’s planned facilities will provide tens of megawatts of computing capacity. One megawatt is enough to power several hundred homes.

Marlowe will use the proceeds from its seed round to finance hardware purchases and hire engineers.

Recent findings suggest that bitcoin has failed to form a higher high for the past 16 days. This is a very long stretch, one that was absent during Bitcoin’s February and June crashes.

It has been revealed that A higher high, in the context of technical analysis, is formed when an asset’s price reaches a upcoming high point above its previous swing high. The absence of higher highs signals that buyers are having a hard time taking back control of the market.

The latest Bitcoin price action adds further to concerns surrounding the future of the flagship cryptocurrency.

Earlier today, BTC crashed to $61,225, its lowest price point in around four and a half months.

Bitcoin's failure to create higher highs despite several attempts to recover reveals that selling pressure remains quite high.

According to recent reports, nevertheless, this technical pattern of 16 days without a higher high does not necessarily spell more pain for Bitcoin. If the cryptocurrency can decisively push above recent resistance zones, it may be a sign that buyers are starting to make a comeback.

Bitcoin is facing persistent withdrawals of huge amounts of money from U.S.-based spot Bitcoin ETFs.

Sources indicate that blackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) witnessed its biggest-ever daily net outflow on Nov. 19.

It has been revealed that the crypto fund suffered a whopping $541.1 million in net withdrawals on the day. At the same time, total net outflows from U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs amounted to around $582.3 million across the entire market.

Recent findings suggest that more alarmingly, the fresh wave of withdrawals brings cumulative net outflows from U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs to around $3.47 billion so far this November.

The ETFs have seen negative net flows on 12 of the first 14 trading days of the month.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mortgage applications increased last week, despite high interest rates, inflation concerns, and a wobbly stock market.
  • According to recent reports, for the week ending Nov.
  • The Purchase Index, which measures the volume of mortgage applications to purchase a single-family home, increased 5% from one week earlier after seasonal adjustment, though purchase applications are down 16% from a year ago.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mortgage applications increased last week, despite high interest rates, inflation concerns, and a wobbly stock market.

According to recent reports, for the week ending Nov. 20, the Mortgage Bankers Association's Market Composite Index—a measure of total mortgage loan application volume—increased 6.1% on a seasonally adjusted basis from one week earlier.

The Purchase Index, which measures the volume of mortgage applications to purchase a single-family home, increased 5% from one week earlier after seasonal adjustment, though purchase applications are down 16% from a year ago.

The average contract interest rate for 30-year fixed mortgages with conforming loan balances jumped to 7.38% this week, an increase from last week's rate of 7.31%, according to MBA calculations, and it's the highest level in five weeks.

Recent findings suggest that A separate survey from Freddie Mac revealed mortgage rates rose to 7.28%, up from  7.11% last week. A year ago at this time, the 30-year fixed-rate mortgage averaged 6.26%.

"While mortgage rates increased slightly on a weekly average basis, rates declined over the course of the week, which likely spurred purchase application activity,” mentioned Joel Kan, MBA’s vice president and deputy chief economist.

“Purchase applications reached their strongest weekly pace since September but remained well behind last year’s pace," he added.

Kan also noted that the share of borrowers relying on riskier adjustable-rate mortgage loans jumped to 11.5%—its highest level in more than a year.

"At 6.39%, the ARM mortgage rate was nearly a full percentage lower than the 30-year fixed rate last week," he said.

According to recent reports, the share of FHA loan applications decreased to 15.9% from 16.1% the prior week. The VA share of total applications decreased to 12.4% from 12.8% the prior week. And the USDA share of total applications remained unchanged at 0.5%.

The refinance share of mortgage activity decreased to 40.1% from 41.1% the previous week, but was 51% lower than the same week one year ago, as homeowners remain locked in to their lower interest rates.

Recent findings suggest that "Refinance activity was flat over the week with conventional applications showing a small increase while VA refinances dropped more than 11%," Kan noted. The latest mortgage application data comes following a week of stock market volatility. On Friday, the Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 briefly plunged into correction territory, defined as a 10% decline from their last peak.

It has been revealed that the sell-off, driven by a wipeout in tech and AI stocks, came a day after Anthropic raised a staggering $81.34 billion during its IPO on Thursday, lifting the company's valuation to $1.414 trillion.Adding to the economic stress was an announcement on Wednesday from President Donald Trump that he's proposed newly introduced tariffs of up to 20% on China, the EU, and a dozen other major U.S. trading partners to take effect next year.

It has been revealed that mortgage rates are calculated based on several economic factors, while your loan term and credit score also influence the mortgage rate you qualify for. On the economic side, rates tend to track the 10-year Treasury note, since most 30-year mortgages are paid off or refinanced in roughly eight to 11 years.

That makes the duration on the loans roughly comparable, and mortgage lenders use the 10-year Treasury as a benchmark for setting rates, adding on a risk premium.

According to recent reports, long-term yields for Treasury notes are determined by a number of factors, including the supply of and demand for U.S. government debt, and investor expectations for inflation over the life of the bonds.

Industry observers note that NEAR Protocol (NEAR) fell 11.41% on Nov. 20 and traded at $2.84, according to TradingView data. In early October, the token was trading near $6, and it has lost about half of its value since then.

In a recent development, over the same period, the volume of NEAR Intents went up. "NEAR went from $6 to $3 in about a month. funny thing is, NEAR Intents is doing more volume now than it did in october," NEAR ecosystem contributor Evgeny Haenko wrote on X on Nov. 20.

According to Haenko, NEAR Intents averaged around $129 million in daily volume in October, and in November it was processing around $134 million a day. "The price got cut in half, the business didn't slow down at all. hard for me to be bearish here," he wrote.

NEAR Intents lets users swap assets across more than 30 blockchains, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana and XRP. The service is built into wallets such as Ledger, Trust Wallet and Brave. Over the past year, its trading volume grew 7.1 times to $39.5 billion.

Recent findings suggest that NEAR Intents has collected about $63 million in fees in total, and the network keeps about 29% of that amount. Fees on the NEAR Intents interface, payments from B2B partners and the spread on better-than-market trades accounted for 16.3%, 9.9% and 2.8% of the fees, respectively. Over the last 30 days, the protocol earned about $1.8 million, compared with $2.2 million in October.

Since February 2026, the protocol has used NEAR Intents revenue to buy NEAR on the market. More than 1.84 million NEAR have gone to the buyback wallet so far, and that is 41.6% of all distributed onchain revenue. Base transaction fees on the network are burned in full.

In early November, the NEAR community also voted to cut the maximum annual issuance from 2.5% to 1.6% over two years. The proposal, HSP-029, went through House of Stake, NEAR's governance initiative, and Haenko is one of its participants.

Industry observers note that on Sept. 29, Bitwise debuted the first U.S. spot NEAR ETF on NYSE Arca under the ticker NRR. Two days later, on Oct. 1, NEAR Intents paused its services after an exploit that cost about $3.8 million, and the team promised to compensate users in full. The exploiter later returned the funds. "The funds from the $3.8M NEAR Intents hack were sent back in full," NEAR Intents general manager Alex Shevchenko said at the time.

While he is consistently bullish on Bitcoin, Kiyosaki is asking investors to be patient and not buy the flagship cryptocurrency before the current crash ends.

"Never grab a falling knife," Kiyosaki warned.

The financial guru suggested that this means investors should wait until the cryptocurrency market crash ends before buying more Bitcoin.

"That means wait for the crash to end….before buying," Kiyosaki elaborated.

Notably, Kiyosaki shared that he began buying Bitcoin when its price was around $20,000 after another major market crash.

The best-selling author hinted that he is planning to do the same during the current market downturn.

"Will wait for Bitcoin bottom again," Kiyosaki noted.

The financial educator reminded his followers of one of his important investment tips.

"Your profit is made when you buy….not when you sell," Kiyosaki noted.

Basically, the financial educator suggested that investors should prioritize finding good entry prices rather than trying to buy Bitcoin while its price keeps dropping.

However, Kiyosaki did not specify a Bitcoin price target or how he is going to know that the market has bottomed out.

Kiyosaki's remarks follow another devastating Bitcoin crash that took the flagship cryptocurrency to its lowest level in more than four months.

On Nov. 20, the world's largest cryptocurrency crashed below the key psychological price level of $60,000 for the first time since July.

According to Reuters, Bitcoin crashed to around $59,381. Bitcoin shed over 3% in a single trading session.

Interestingly, BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) saw a record $541.1 million in daily outflows.

Overall, the latest data shows that November has seen total net outflows from U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs worth around $3.47 billion.

Interestingly, Kiyosaki has shared his excitement about buying Bitcoin during major market corrections several times.

According to recent reports, earlier, on Nov. 20, Kiyosaki described the ongoing market crash as a possible buying opportunity. He suggested that experienced investors are sitting back and waiting to accumulate while bad investors are trying to sell everything.

"I am most excited about Bitcoin's crash. Waiting to buy more," Kiyosaki declared.

We had a party at the hospital and watched the sun come up after he was born. The transition has felt very natural. The house has been crowded with family giving so much love and support. The new dad added, "Brooks is an old English name, and I’m English, so it ties to my roots. My oldest son Adler wanted to name him River, so we took a variation of that which refers to a harmonious, running body of water which flows and connects life.”.

In a recent development, page Six previously revealed that while Richards was attending the Maison D’Or cocktail launch in Los Angeles over the weekend, she reportedly told the outlet, “I’m on baby watch right now. Then, according to the outlet, someone later asked Richards if Aldjufrie was in labor, to which she replied, "I think so.".

“I’ve been calling to make sure this is not a false alarm because I’m gonna call the hospital to make sure that she gets right in and has a room because, you know, we’re very close to the hospital,” Hilton told the outlet.

"We will not be in Aspen this year because my sister is giving birth any day now. So we're not going to make her get on a plane and fly to Aspen," Alexia added.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Charles Hoskinson’s Cardano-linked privacy blockchain Midnight has inked a significant initial deal with a Japanese payments firm as it aims to make further inroads into traditional finance.

The news comes soon after a key breakthrough for Midnight in the United Kingdom, where Monument Bank started tokenizing customer deposits on the blockchain.

Per a Nov. 19 NADA NEWS report, Midnight Foundation President Fahmi Syed remarked the foundation had inked an MOU (memorandum of understanding) with a major Japanese payments tech giant.

In a recent development, syed did not name the firm. But the deal is a big one for Midnight’s bid to establish a presence in Japan’s financial services sector.

However, it is just an initial agreement, and no commercial services have been rolled out in Japan yet.

It is also worth noting that the Midnight Foundation is talking to some major Japanese banks and companies working with intellectual property and medical data.

According to Syed, he spent two days in Tokyo meeting with major financial institutions and other companies.

Japan has been a key market for Midnight, along with the United States.

According to Midnight Foundation Japan country manager Taro Kimura, Japan is the only Asian country where the foundation has a local representative on the ground.

Midnight has been eyeing Japan more keenly due to the country’s sizeable Cardano community.

The Japanese push comes hot on the heels of a historic development in the British banking sector.

Industry observers note that on Nov. 18, British financial institution Monument Bank started tokenizing retail customer deposits on Midnight. It is the first UK bank to launch such a product on a public blockchain.

Sources indicate that the first phase of the venture involves up to £250 million in tokenized deposits. For this, the bank is offering customers a 12-month fixed annual interest rate of 5.2%.

Recent findings suggest that midnight employs zero-knowledge cryptography to safeguard sensitive transaction details, unlike traditional public blockchains. As a result, banks can meet compliance requirements while keeping their customers’ private information and transaction details out of public view.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that artificial intelligence tooling startup Epochal AI Inc.
  • Sources indicate that the capital was provided by Chief Executive Officer Guodong Zhang, a machine learning researcher who earlier co-founded xAI Corp.
  • In a recent development, epochal’s first offering is a cloud service called the Epochal Time Portal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 20:30 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

Recent findings suggest that artificial intelligence tooling startup Epochal AI Inc. launched today with $100 million in funding.

Sources indicate that the capital was provided by Chief Executive Officer Guodong Zhang, a machine learning researcher who earlier co-founded xAI Corp. He established Epochal earlier this year with two other xAI co-founders, Zihang Dai and Manuel Kroiss. The tech giant’s staff also includes former researchers from Anthropic PBC, OpenAI Group PBC and Google DeepMind.

In a recent development, epochal’s first offering is a cloud service called the Epochal Time Portal. According to the company, it enables developers to train AI models that can predict future events. The service does so by providing models with access to historical web data from the past 30 years.

If a bank wishes to train an AI that can predict quarterly earnings, it could use the service to fetch financial results from the first three quarters of 2025. It could then ask the AI to estimate fourth-quarter results from the same year.

After the model generates its predictions, developers can compare them against real fourth-quarter earnings to check the model’s accuracy. They can make adjustments if necessary and then repeat the training workflow until the model starts generating accurate forecasts.

It has been revealed that the Epochal Time Portal features more than 1 trillion historical web pages on launch. Each entry includes a timestamp that indicates when it was created. According to the tech giant, its timestamps make it possible to track how a web page changed over time.

AI models access the content through a purpose-built search engine. It enables them to specify the time periods from which they wish to retrieve web pages. According to Epochal, its platform provides one-minute granularity for the most frequently updated pages.

Sources indicate that like consumer search engines, the Epochal Time Portal prioritizes the web pages that are most relevant to each given query. The difference is that it considers web pages’ creation date when evaluating relevance. If a query contains the term “Meta” but asks for pages created before 2021, the year Facebook Inc. rebranded, the Epochal Time Portal will not bring up pages that relate to the social networking giant.

Today’s frontier models can determine that they’re being trained on historical data rather than up-to-date information. For example, a model might compare the creation date of a web page to the virtual clock of the operating system on which it deployed. Such discrepancies can lower the effectiveness of training runs.

According to Epochal, its service mitigates the concern by deploying AI models in sandboxes synced to their training data. If a firm is training a model on we pages from 2025, the Epochal Time Portal will run it on a Linux version from that year. It applies the same precautions to the software tools and programming language versions that models use.

The Epochal Time Portal is initially available in a single free tier with low usage limits. Epochal plans to follow up the launch by sharing the results of several AI experiments that its researchers have carried out using the service.

Bitcoin has struggled to turn its latest price rebound into a lasting recovery. Buyers briefly pushed BTC above $64,000, but then reversed the gain, sending Bitcoin back below $60,000.

It has been revealed that blackRock’s IBIT accounted for $509.3 million of Monday’s $569.7 million Bitcoin ETF outflow. The fund’s withdrawals alone contributed almost 90% of the day’s total, making it the biggest driver of the sell-off.

Glassnode’s supply-in-profit metric fell to 46%, down from 54.2% one week earlier. The shift means most circulating Bitcoin is now held outside the profit category, marking a sharp deterioration in market profitability.

The change is substantial and maybe bad at the same time because it alters how investors may react to another drop. Holders who were comfortably sitting on gains can wait out volatility. Those who have watched their positions turn red may instead use the next rebound to reduce exposure.

Short-term holders are facing difficult conditions, with net unrealized profit and loss reportedly dropping to negative 18.3% as pressure mounts on coins acquired more recently. Realized losses have also climbed as investors sell below their acquisition prices.
